title: ephemeral-slowpath-fallback-weighted-penalty-cooldown-hotfix
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: Hotfix: Add telemetry-driven soft-deny cooldown to reduce slowpath thrashing during regional slowdowns; include new metrics and dashboard; update docs and tests.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed repeated slowpath thrashing in small regional spikes where tenants would rapidly oscillate between normal admission and slowpath fallback. That behavior caused elevated p99 tail latencies and KV cache churn during short-lived node slowdowns. This PR adds a telemetry-backed, ephemeral weighted-penalty cooldown that gates slowpath fallthroughs for tenants and routes, smoothing oscillations without permanently favoring any tenant. Intended as a focused hotfix for release/v1.42 to mitigate production noise and buy time for a longer-term scheduling improvement.

What this changes (single-line summary): Introduce PenaltyManager with per-tenant weighted penalty decay, wire telemetry signals into the admission controller, add a short soft-deny window (configurable) with exponential cooldown, and ship dashboards and integration tests. Also include conservative defaults and a fast opt-out toggle for customers using Dedicated/Private.

Key design notes: - Penalty units are charged when a request falls back to slowpath due to resource pressure or explicit circuit decisions. The unit is weighted by request cost (token estimate + KV impact). - PenaltyManager exposes a remaining_penalty float [0..1] per tenant/route. Admission controller multiplies slowpath acceptance probability by (1 - remaining_penalty) during the soft-deny window. - Decay uses an exponential backoff: penalty_t = penalty_0 * exp(-t / tau), with tau configurable per deployment tier. - Telemetry thresholds derive from the serving runtime's slowpath_error_rate and kv_drain_ratio metrics over a short sliding window (30s). We purposely avoid coupling to long-lived aggregates to keep reactions local and fast.

Commits (summary): - 8c9d2ab: introduce penalty manager core + in-memory store + unit tests - 1f4b7e0: admission controller integration and soft-deny evaluation - e22f4b3: telemetry hooks + mappings and sampled tags for tenant/route - 4a7b2c1: add integration test reproducer and CI job - 9a1c6f0: docs and operational runbook + dashboard YAML - bf3e4d2: compatibility note for private installer and opt-out flag

Files changed (high level): - pkg/serving/slowpath controlador.go: admission path updated to consult PenaltyManager and apply probabilistic soft-deny. Small, contained change with clear feature flag. - pkg/serving/penalty/penalty_manager.go: new package implementing charges, decay, and a small LRU to bound memory. - pkg/telemetry/metrics/telemetry_mappings.go: map existing slowpath and kv metrics to the penalty trigger. - internal/sre/telemetry_dashboards.yaml: new SLO-focused dashboard panels (penalty heatmap, per-tenant decay curves). - integration-tests/slowpath_repro: new repro and deterministic test using stubbed metrics. - docs/operational/soft-deny-windows.md: runbook + troubleshooting.

Backward/forward compatibility: The feature is behind a runtime feature flag enabled on release/v1.42 for the rollout cohort. The opt-out flag lives in config/deploy and is documented for Private/Dedicated customers. Telemetry mappings are additive and rely on existing metric names; where name drift exists the patch includes a compatibility shim (deploy/patches/telemetry-migration-compat.md).

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for PenaltyManager decay math and admission gating (pkg/serving/penalty/*). Integration repro runs in CI with a new deterministic slowpath test that stubs the telemetry feed to emulate 30s spikes. CI initially failed on a flaky timing assumption in tests; fixed by switching to virtualized clock in the integration harness. Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration, e2e smoke).

Performance and resource considerations: The LRU size is conservative (default 10k tenants) with an upper bound guard; memory usage for the penalty store is negligible relative to the runtime (~2MB at default). The admission check is a single in-process lookup + float math; microbenchmarks showed <1% added CPU on the critical path at 1000rps.

Rollback plan: Feature flag gating allows safe rollback by disabling the soft-deny window. If a rollback is required post-deploy we will revert the feature flag and optionally flush penalty state; a brief out-of-band job can clear the LRU if needed.

Review conversation (highlights): - Aisha: "Can we avoid tenant starvation when penalty accumulates across multiple short spikes?" Reply (author): "We cap accumulated penalty per epoch and add a decay floor — the decay tau is shorter for transient tiers; added test coverage to assert no permanent starvation." - Claire: "Telemetry mapping needs a compatibility note for older private installs." Reply: "Added telemetry-migration-compat.md and a config toggle; private installer will include the shim in the next non-critical release." - Tom: "Integration repro timed out on CI initially." Reply: "Fixed by switching to a virtual clock and reducing wall-clock waits — see commit 4a7b2c1." Approvals: Aisha, Claire approved after small nits were addressed. Tom gave final +1.

Operational notes and dashboards: New panels added to SRE dashboards showing per-tenant penalty heatmap, global slowpath trigger rate, KV drain ratio, and effective acceptance probability. Pager trigger adjusted: we avoid new alerts for penalty charge events; instead we alert on sustained (>3m) global slowpath rate increase.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Instead of hard circuit flips or coarse global throttles, this PR implements a short-lived, telemetry-anchored smoothing mechanism that probabilistically gates slowpath acceptance. It reduces oscillation without imposing long-term restrictions and is lightweight to roll back.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to release/v1.42 on 2026-02-18 after CI green and approvals. Backported notes: included a minimal backport to 1.41 branch as a separate patch for a customer experiencing repeated p99 spikes; that backport is tracked in ENG-4730.

Follow-ups: - ENG-4799: evaluate adding cross-node penalty replication for very large tenant footprints (design doc stubbed). - ENG-4801: consider adding a small multiclass penalty weight based on model and route cost. - Cleanup: remove telemetry compatibility shim after 3 releases.
